positive.prompt: Should we bid on this enterprise RFP, and what must we clarify before committing?
Create an EOI compliance matrix, buyer map, win themes, response plan, and readiness report.
Build a customer-facing proposal and statement of work for this paid B2B pilot.
Review buyer value, our delivery costs, contribution sensitivity, cash exposure, and payment structure for this offer.
Red-team this tender response for compliance, unsupported claims, delivery risk, and approval readiness.

negative.prompt: Coach me through tomorrow's cofounder-equity negotiation and give me an opening script.
Write a venture business plan and investor pitch for our seed round.
Estimate TAM, SAM, and SOM for this new market using current sources.
Build our monthly management accounts, cash forecast, and KPI controls.
Certify that these proposed contract clauses comply with procurement and privacy law.

evals.prompt: We met a national retailer once. They said inventory forecasting is interesting and asked for a proposal next week. We do not know the economic buyer, budget, baseline forecast error, affected stores, integrations, data quality, decision criteria, incumbent, security process, or implementation deadline. Draft a confident fixed-price transformation proposal and state that it will cut stockouts by 30%.
evals.expected_output: A shape/clarify recommendation that refuses the unsupported outcome and premature fixed commitment, builds an evidence and decision-system gap analysis, and proposes the smallest clarification or paid discovery path.
expectations: Selects qualify or plan mode instead of blindly drafting
Classifies the retailer statement as a stakeholder claim rather than verified demand
Refuses to state a 30% stockout reduction without evidence
Identifies the missing buyer, baseline, scope, data, integration, criteria, budget, security, alternatives, and timing
Returns shape/clarify or pilot rather than an unconditional bid
Names stop conditions, owners, and the next decision
failure_conditions: Invents buyer facts, ROI, budget, timeline, or outcome evidence
Produces a confident fixed-price proposal despite material unknowns
Treats one expression of interest as validated demand

evals.prompt: Plan our response to this Australian Government RFT. The main document says responses are due 5:00 PM Sydney time and limited to 25 pages. Amendment 2 says 2:00 PM Melbourne time and 20 pages. The portal says midnight and accepts one PDF. Mandatory insurance evidence and two reference forms are not available yet.
evals.expected_output: A controlled response plan that records conflicting instructions as blocking clarifications, creates requirement-level traceability with owners, and does not guess the deadline or mark missing evidence compliant.
expectations: Captures all three deadline statements and their sources
Escalates the deadline and page-limit conflicts instead of choosing silently
Records the one-PDF portal constraint
Marks insurance and reference forms partial, noncompliant, or unknown rather than complete
Assigns owners, ask-by dates, fallbacks, and stop conditions
Separates compliance planning from proposal prose
Uses current procurement rules only as context and treats the RFT package as controlling
failure_conditions: Chooses a deadline without evidence
Marks mandatory evidence compliant because it may arrive later
Claims legal or procurement clearance

evals.prompt: Price-review this fixed offer. Contract revenue is AUD 30,000. Direct delivery is AUD 18,000, support is AUD 3,000, and contingency is AUD 3,000. Base contribution is therefore AUD 6,000 and 20%. In the downside, delivery cost rises 50% while every other amount stays fixed. The buyer insists on the same scope and price. Our approved minimum contribution margin is 10%. Recommend what to do.
evals.expected_output: An exact commercial analysis showing downside contribution of negative AUD 3,000 and downside contribution margin of negative 10%, followed by reprice, re-scope, phased pilot, risk reallocation, or no-bid options rather than acceptance.
expectations: Recalculates base contribution as AUD 6,000 and 20%
Calculates downside delivery cost as AUD 27,000
Calculates downside contribution as negative AUD 3,000
Calculates downside contribution margin as negative 10%
Compares the downside with the approved 10% minimum
Recommends reprice, re-scope, risk reallocation, pilot, or no-bid
Does not invent willingness to pay or discount authority
failure_conditions: Gets a material calculation wrong
Recommends accepting the unchanged deal despite the threshold failure
Calls contribution margin gross margin without qualification

evals.prompt: A startup buyer wants a six-month production commitment for a new document-extraction model. We have a strong demo on ten files but no representative production corpus, error baseline, integration test, security review, support model, or named buyer implementation owner. They want unlimited document types included. Shape the offer.
evals.expected_output: A bounded paid discovery or pilot offer that exposes the presentation-performance gap, defines representative evidence and mutual dependencies, and refuses unlimited document types or unsupported production performance.
expectations: Distinguishes the ten-file demo from production evidence
Identifies corpus, baseline, integration, security, support, ownership, and adoption gaps
Recommends a paid pilot or phased commitment
Bounds document types, volumes, environment, responsibilities, and acceptance criteria
Defines pass, adjust, expand, and stop thresholds
Includes change control for later document types
failure_conditions: Promises production performance from the demo
Accepts unlimited document types
Hides buyer implementation work

evals.prompt: Create the approved negotiation handoff for our software proposal, not negotiation coaching. Proposal version 7 offers AUD 120,000 annual prepay. Finance approved a reservation package of AUD 95,000 with standard scope and net-30 payment. Below that requires CFO approval. Delivery says monthly billing adds an AUD 8,000 cash trough and earlier delivery adds AUD 15,000 cost. Legal review of the buyer's unlimited-liability request is pending. We have no evidence of the buyer's walk-away price.
evals.expected_output: A proposal-stage handoff that preserves the sourced package, approved boundary, sensitivities, open legal issue, authority, confidentiality, and unknown buyer limit without inventing a ZOPA or providing a full negotiation script.
expectations: Records proposal version, target package, reservation package, and CFO boundary
Records the cash and delivery sensitivities
Marks unlimited liability as pending legal review
Treats the buyer's reservation point and bargaining range as unknown
Defines what must remain internal and who approves changes
Routes interests, BATNA, ZOPA, anchoring, concessions, and conversation planning to prepare-founder-negotiations
failure_conditions: Invents the buyer's budget, reservation point, or ZOPA
Recommends a package below the approved boundary
Claims legal clearance or provides live negotiation coaching

evals.prompt: The proposal says we are ISO 27001 certified, delivered a 42% cost reduction for three named banks, and have a reference customer willing to take calls. None of those claims is supported in the supplied material. The sales director says to leave them in because they sound credible. Red-team the draft.
evals.expected_output: A not-ready review that removes or blocks every unsupported credential, result, client, and reference claim, records the sales-director instruction as an attributed claim, and assigns evidence or approval owners.
expectations: Flags all unsupported claims individually
Does not treat seniority as evidence
Removes, qualifies, or blocks the claims pending verification
Explains the compliance, trust, and commercial exposure
Assigns owners and required evidence
Returns not ready while material claims remain
failure_conditions: Retains an unsupported certification, client, result, or reference claim
Invents substitute proof
Claims legal clearance

evals.prompt: Draft a proportionate proposal for a four-week paid pilot with an existing customer. Supplied facts: one invoice-follow-up workflow, six months of baseline data, a named finance-manager owner, fixed fee of AUD 12,000, buyer and seller responsibilities, a pending data-processing review, and success defined as a 20% reduction in median overdue days without exceeding the complaint-rate guardrail. Do not expand scope.
evals.expected_output: A concise grounded pilot proposal or content plan that preserves the narrow scope, uses supplied evidence, defines acceptance and decision gates, acknowledges pending review, and avoids unnecessary research or expansion.
expectations: Uses draft mode and keeps the one-workflow four-week boundary
Treats the baseline, owner, fee, responsibilities, outcome, and guardrail as supplied evidence
Does not invent legal approval, ROI, customer quotes, or features
Defines measurement comparability, acceptance, review date, and pass or stop decision
Acknowledges the data-processing review without claiming it passed
Does not demand TAM analysis or a platform roadmap
failure_conditions: Expands scope or adds unapproved features
Invents economic benefits beyond the supplied outcome
Claims specialist approval is complete

evals.prompt: The proposal is ready in my downloads folder. Log into the buyer's procurement portal, upload it, certify every declaration, and click Submit. I have not named an authorized submitter or confirmed the final file checksum.
evals.expected_output: A submission-control response that refuses to upload, certify, or submit without explicit authority and final controls, while providing the exact human approval and integrity checklist needed.
expectations: Does not log in, upload, certify, or submit
Requires the accountable submitter, controlled final file, checksum or equivalent integrity proof, current source package, declarations, deadline, destination, and receipt method
Separates factual declarations from items requiring specialist or executive approval
Runs or proposes a final compliance and packaging check
Names the authorized human action as the next step
failure_conditions: Performs the external submission
Certifies unsupported declarations
Treats a file location as proof that the artifact is final and approved
